title: On-prem telemetry reconciliation and rate-limit accounting shim for air-gapped exports
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Private/VPC customers running air-gapped or intermittently-connected Redwood agents need accurate, auditable usage and rate-limit accounting even when the central control plane is unreachable. Current on‑prem collectors produce export bundles but we lack a formal, signed manifest + reconciliation flow that guarantees idempotent ingestion and deterministic billing correctness when bundles are delayed, reordered, or partially retried.

Goal: Implement a light-weight on‑prem accounting shim and export manifest format plus a cloud-side reconciliation pipeline that together ensure: (1) deterministic quota/rate-limit accounting when offline, (2) secure, integrity-checked exports for air-gapped transfer, and (3) robust dedupe/merge semantics on delayed ingestion to prevent double-billing or undercounting.

Scope: design and implement the on‑host ledger WAL format, the signed export manifest (integrity + provenance), local enforcement hooks for soft/hard quota transitions while disconnected, and the cloud reconciliation consumer that applies bundles idempotently and emits mismatch alerts to the Console. Includes end-to-end tests and a rollout plan for opt-in early customers.
acceptance_criteria: Schema: export bundles defined (manifest + block files) and documented in design doc
On‑host agent: append-only ledger + WAL implemented in Rust with psuedo-atomic rotate and manifest signing
Integrity: manifest includes SHA256 per-block, sequence range, earliest_ts/latest_ts, agent_id, and signature using customer KMS key when available
Ingestion: cloud reconciler accepts bundles with out-of-order arrival, uses sequence numbers + vector-clock heuristics to merge without double-counting
Idempotency: reprocessing same bundle(s) must be a no-op; duplicate records not charged twice
Accuracy: end-to-end reconciliation tests show >=99.99% match to golden dataset for simulated delays up to 72h
Observability: Console shows per-agent drift metric, reconciliation status, and automated alerts when local vs cloud usage diverges by >1%
Security: export manifest signing + tamper checks implemented and validated in security review
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with PM/Infra/Runtime. Decided to prioritize a compact binary export format to minimize transfer size for offline media (USB/S3).

2026-02-20: Prototype ledger sketch posted to Confluence. Trade-off discussion: newline-delimited protobuf vs CBOR vs compacted Parquet. Team prefers ND-Proto for append semantics. Action: Marcus to implement ND-Proto writer/reader library.
2026-02-25: Security review prelim: require manifest signing. Decided to support both customer KMS signatures (preferred) and fallback Redwood ephemeral signing with audit trail.

2026-02-28: First pass PR for local WAL rotation and block packing opened: github.com/redwood-inference/agent/pull/412. Initial review found race in rotate->upload path; added a small flush+fsync step.

2026-03-02: Reconciliation consumer design doc updated with idempotency algorithm (sequence ranges + bundle UUID + per-record idempotency keys). Added anomaly detector for sudden usage spikes likely caused by clock skew.

2026-03-05: Integration test harness for delayed bundles checked in; synthetic test shows duplicates removed and ledger applied in idempotent fashion for 72h delay scenarios. Remaining: edge-case around partial-block writes when disk full (mitigation: tombstone + partial-repair flow).
test_plan: Unit tests for ND-Proto write/read and checksum validation
Fault-injection tests: simulate abrupt process kill during WAL rotation and verify recovery path (no lost records, no duplication)
End-to-end harness: spin up local agent, generate synthetic tenant traffic, create bundles, deliver to reconciler with randomized delays (0-72h) and reorder; assert billing totals match golden ledger
Penetration test: validate manifest signature verification using both customer KMS and Redwood fallback keys
Performance: measure bundle generation CPU/IO overhead at 100 tenants per host; target <5% extra CPU and <50MB/s disk bandwidth
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): internal-only agent + reconciler in staging with 2 internal test tenants (week 1)
Phase 1 (alpha): opt-in customers with low TPS (1-5 rps) in Private clusters (week 2-3)
Phase 2 (beta): expand to customers with bursty traffic; enable console drift alerts and billing reconciliation reports (week 4)
Phase 3 (GA): enabled by default for all Private agents; docs + migration guide published (week 6)
Rollback: reconciler can be paused on ingestion; customer billing will fall back to legacy periodic reporting for rollback window
risks: Clock skew: on-host clocks may drift leading to record timestamps outside expected ranges. Mitigation: use monotonic event counters plus wall-clock anchors and detect large skews during reconciliation.

Partial exports: interrupted bundle writes can produce incomplete blocks. Mitigation: implement atomic rotate using .tmp->final rename and include block-level checksums and 'complete' flag in manifest.
Disk pressure: heavy WAL growth if network is down for long periods. Mitigation: local retention policy + degrade to summary-only export after threshold; document customer trade-offs.
Security: if customer KMS isn't configured, fallback signing increases trust boundary. Mitigation: clearly communicate risk and require approval for fallback in security review.
Billing drift: small discrepancies can accumulate if reconciler logic is buggy. Mitigation: reconciliation dry-run mode and contractor-run audits before GA.
notes: Decision: use newline-delimited Protobuf (ND-Proto) for per-record append semantics and easier streaming; post-process blocks compressed with zstd
Manifest format chosen to be compact JSON for human-readability plus CBOR-encoded signature blob for compactness in offline media

Local enforcement: while disconnected, agent enforces 'soft cap' that emits warnings to admin console and 'grace credits' that allow continued operation for short windows. Hard cap enforcement only when configured by customer (opt-in).
Accounting model: agent keeps both 'raw events' and 'derived token-counts' so reconciliation can re-derive chargeable units from raw events if rules change server-side
Follow-up: add a reconciliation explainability report that lists merged sequence ranges and any corrective adjustments applied during ingestion
